arguments.value: This agreement is between Immunotolerance, Inc. and Alan Crane. Crane will provide consulting, advisory, and related services that the company reasonably requests, including the services described on Schedule A, and he agrees not to compete in the defined field during the consultation period and for one year after it ends. The agreement starts on the effective date and lasts for four years, then renews automatically for one-year periods unless the company gives 90 days’ notice. As compensation, and subject to board approval and a restricted stock agreement, the company will issue and sell Crane 1,990,000 shares of common stock for $190 total, and it will reimburse reasonable, documented out-of-pocket expenses; Crane is not entitled to employee benefits. The company may end the consultation period for cause, and Crane may terminate with 30 days’ written notice. Crane must protect the company’s confidential information, return company property, assign inventions made in connection with the services or based on company confidential information to the company, and not solicit the company’s employees during the agreement and for one year afterward. The agreement says Massachusetts law governs it.
